blocks.prompt: 17. If \(\frac{1}{a}, \frac{1}{b}\) and \(\frac{1}{c}\) are in A.P., show that \(b = \frac{2ac}{a + c}\).
blocks.explanation:
A proof: three numbers are in A.P., so we use 'twice the middle = sum of the other two'.
We must make \(b\) the subject.
Plan: write the condition, add the fractions on the right, then take reciprocals.
steps:
Given: \(\frac{1}{a}, \frac{1}{b}, \frac{1}{c}\) are in A.P. (\(a, b, c \ne 0\))
To prove: \(b = \frac{2ac}{a + c}\).
Method: \(2 \times \text{middle} = \text{first} + \text{last}\).

Write the A.P. condition
\[\dfrac{2}{b} = \dfrac{1}{a} + \dfrac{1}{c}\]
Why: \(\frac{1}{b} - \frac{1}{a} = \frac{1}{c} - \frac{1}{b}\) rearranges to this.

Add the fractions
\[\dfrac{2}{b} = \dfrac{c + a}{ac}\]
Why: Common denominator \(ac\).

Take reciprocals
\[\dfrac{b}{2} = \dfrac{ac}{a + c}\]
\[b = \dfrac{2ac}{a + c}\]
Why: If two non-zero fractions are equal, their reciprocals are equal. Then multiply by 2.

Check with numbers
Take \(a = 1,\ c = 3\): \(b = \frac{2(3)}{4} = \frac{3}{2}\)
\[\tfrac{1}{1},\ \tfrac{2}{3},\ \tfrac{1}{3}:\ \text{gaps } -\tfrac{1}{3},\ -\tfrac{1}{3} \;\checkmark\]
Why: The reciprocals are in A.P. for the \(b\) given by the formula.
